validation.summary: 3 defect(s) detected. Structural score: 1.000. Coverage score: 0.946. Hallucination score: 1.000. Semantic score: 1.000. Overall score: 0.946.

review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers many core use cases, but it still has several semantic omissions and a few unsupported behaviors. The biggest issues are missing inventory-asset-addition coverage for R11-R13 and an unsupported IT/location-creation path drawn as if performed by User. There are also some requirement mismatches around request approval and report generation detail.

defects.description: Requirement R11 is still not represented by a diagram element: the diagram does not show DA group members or authorised inventory group members adding department-owned inventory assets.
defects.evidence: R11 requires: 'Any DA group member or authorised inventory group member can add inventory assets owned by the department.' The diagram's add-asset flow (N18-N27) only models an unspecified User/Inventory system path for creating a new asset and an exception path for missing type. It does not show the required actors or department-owned restriction.
defects.suggested_action: Add a modeled path for DA group member / authorised inventory group member adding department-owned assets, or connect the existing add-asset flow to this requirement explicitly.

defects.description: Requirement R12 is still not represented by a diagram element: the diagram does not show faculty members adding related-department inventory.
defects.evidence: R12 requires: 'Any faculty member can add all related departments inventory.' The current diagram has no faculty-member branch or equivalent actor/condition in the add-asset section (N18-N27).
defects.suggested_action: Add a branch or swimlane path for faculty members adding related-department inventory.

defects.description: Requirement R13 is still not represented by a diagram element: the diagram does not show university group members adding all assets in the inventory.
defects.evidence: R13 requires: 'Any university group member can add all assets in the inventory.' The diagram's add-asset flow only shows a generic User adding a new asset, which is not the same required permission scope or actor group.
defects.suggested_action: Add a university-group path for adding inventory assets, or map the existing add-asset action to that actor and permission scope.

defects.description: The diagram draws IT/new-location actions as performed by User, which conflicts with the requirement that IT group members create a new space and modify floor structure after an exception request from an administrative level.
defects.evidence: R18 states: 'IT group members can create a new space and modify floor structure when they receive an exception request from any administrative level.' The diagram routes the exception path to N25 'Send exception request' and then has N26 'Create new space' and N27 'Modify floor structure' in the [User] lane, not an IT group lane. N61 'Create exception request' is also in the User lane, but the requirement makes IT the performer of the creation/modification steps.
defects.suggested_action: Move the 'create new space' and 'modify floor structure' actions to the Inventory system lane only if it represents IT group behavior, and show the exception request being received from an administrative-level source.

defects.description: The approval flow does not clearly implement the required approval/execution sequence: approved requests should be added to a waiting-for-execution list, and inventory is updated when the user receives the requested asset.
defects.evidence: R19 requires approval by administration-level or authorised inventory member, R21 says the request is added to the waiting-for-execution list, and R22 says inventory is updated when the user receives the requested asset. The diagram shows N39 'Display pending request list', N40 'Approve request', N41 'Notify user by email', but there is no explicit waiting-for-execution list state and no explicit 'receive requested asset' event preceding the inventory update. N34-N38 similarly create/check/update without showing the required execution queue semantics.
defects.suggested_action: Add an explicit step/state for adding the approved request to the waiting-for-execution list and a separate execution/receipt step before inventory is updated.

defects.description: The report use case is modeled too generically: the diagram displays and filters/sorts a report, but it does not distinguish the three required report types as produced outputs.
defects.evidence: R27-R29 require the system to produce an asset-by-location report, a request report, and a user-permission report. The diagram has N49 'Display report types' and N50 'Display report' with generic filter/sort steps, but no explicit branching or representation of the three distinct report outputs.
defects.suggested_action: Model separate report branches or clearly label the generic report step as one of the three required report types, with all three types explicitly reachable.

strengths: Authentication is modeled with a username/password entry and success/failure path.
The modify-asset scenario includes search, edit, missing-asset, and insufficient-privilege outcomes.
The request-creation flow includes basic and advanced request form variants.
The transfer flows cover same-department, inter-department, inter-faculty, and outside-university cases at a high level.
unsupported_behaviors: N26 and N27 are drawn as User actions for IT-owned location-creation behavior required by R18.
The diagram implies generic report handling without explicit asset-report/request-report/user-permission-report outputs required by R27-R29.
